name: Tail-Risk Put Hedge
summary: A small, persistent allocation to deep OTM long-dated puts that pay off only in a crash, sized as a standing insurance premium.
max_profit: (strike - 0) x 100 - premium, in a total collapse; practically, 10-30x the premium in a >20% crash
max_loss: premium paid (expected to be lost in most quarters)

greeks.gamma: small but explosive on a big move
greeks.vega: strongly positive - this is primarily a long-vol position

when_to_use: As a standing overlay on a share portfolio, sized at 0.3-0.6% of portfolio value per quarter. Buy when VIX < 16 and IV Rank <= 25; skip or reduce when IV Rank > 50 (crash insurance is already expensive).
entry_rules: Budget: total annual premium spend <= 2% of portfolio value. At $50k that is $1,000/yr, ~$250/quarter.
Strike by delta in [0.05, 0.10]; prefer index/ETF puts (SPY, QQQ) over single names for cost efficiency.
Require IV Rank <= 30 and VIX <= 18 at purchase; if above, halve the size.
Require OI >= 500 (far OTM strikes are thin).
Reject if ask - bid > 15% of mid.
management_rules: Roll at 45-60 DTE to a new 90-180 DTE 0.05-0.10 delta strike; do not hold into the steep theta zone.

MONETIZATION RULE: if the put's value reaches 5x the premium paid, sell half and re-strike the remainder lower. If it reaches 10x, sell all and re-establish a new tail hedge with a fraction of the proceeds.
Increase the hedge notional after a large rally (when it is cheap), reduce it after a crash (when it is expensive) - explicitly contrarian.
Accept that 90%+ of these expire worthless; do not 'fix' the strategy after a losing year.
exit_rules: Close before expiration if ITM to avoid auto-exercise into a short-share obligation on a put the account does not have shares for (if the puts exceed the share position, exercise creates SHORT stock).
Abandon (let expire worthless) OTM puts with value < 0.05 - transaction costs exceed the residual.
assignment_risk: No short leg. The hazard is auto-exercise of a deep ITM long put at expiry: if the number of puts exceeds the number of 100-share lots owned, exercise creates a short stock position. Always close rather than exercise.
liquidity_needs: Index ETF options only; far OTM single-name puts are too wide.
common_mistakes: Sizing the hedge so large that its bleed exceeds the portfolio's expected return; buying after the crash starts; never monetizing and giving back the entire payoff.
zero_dte_notes: 0DTE tail puts are a different trade entirely (intraday crash lottery); they do not hedge a portfolio over time.
family: Stock/ETF Shares Combined With Options (covered writes, protective hedges, collars, synthetics, repairs, conversions)
